title: Qwen3.6-27B dense SiLU gate-plane scratch alias

hardware.primary: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX / gfx1100 / HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 / PCI 0000:10:00.0 / sysfs card0 / 23.984375 GiB VRAM
hardware.safeguard: AMD Radeon Pro W7900 / gfx1100 / HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 / PCI 0000:0d:00.0 / sysfs card1 / 44.984375 GiB VRAM

implementation.problem: Dense prefill reserved an independent BF16 FFN intermediate even though SiLU consumes gate/up elementwise and the gate plane is dead after that operation.
implementation.change: Make separate SiLU gate/output alias-safe, view ffn_intermediate over the first half of ffn_gate_up, and teach the single-arena planner the distinct gate-half and up-half physical lifetimes.
implementation.scope: The alias is admitted only by an existing model-scoped dense liveness policy using the single-arena grouping. MoE, diagnostics, peer GDN modes, and owner-slot arenas retain their prior layouts.

red_green.red: The dense 768-row fixture gave ffn_intermediate a distinct pointer; direct 4096-row planning retained a 495.315-MiB physical bulk-prefill scratch.
red_green.green: ffn_intermediate is the exact first-half view of ffn_gate_up, subrange-aware conflict checks reject every undeclared live overlap, and the direct 4096-row physical scratch is 474.690 MiB.
red_green.hip_exact_bit_oracle: A live gfx1100 test writes BF16 SiLU(gate)*up back over gate for 7x259 elements and matches the host BF16-bit oracle exactly.

protocol.hipengine: Selector-unset package-default sole-T16 session, repeated token 9707, one discarded warmup plus three measured persistent reset/replays, bulk prefill, BF16 KV, HIP graph decode, 128 timed transitions, cached compiler artifacts.
protocol.whole_device_memory: 5 ms sysfs VRAM samples around the complete child process. Peak delta is peak minus pre-process baseline.
protocol.command_template: env -u HIPENGINE_GGUF_GDN_PREFILL_MODE -u HIPENGINE_GGUF_Q4_T16_SELECTED_PREFILL_MODE -u HIPENGINE_GGUF_LINEAR_ATTN_CONV_PREFILL_MODE -u HIPENGINE_GGUF_PREFILL_ROUTER_SELECT_THREADS -u HIPENGINE_GGUF_PREFILL_DEVICE_METADATA HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 HIPENGINE_HIP_ARCH=gfx1100 HIPENGINE_COMPILER_VERSION_FILE=/tmp/hipengine-qwen36-27b-single-layout-hipcc-version.txt HIPENGINE_REQUIRE_CACHED_BUILD=1 PYTHONPATH=. /home/lhl/mambaforge/envs/therock/bin/python scripts/qwen35_gguf_bench.py --model /models/gguf/Qwen3.6-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf --quant gguf_q4_k_m --token-id 9707 --prompt-length <512|1024|4096|8192> --decode-tokens 128 --warmup-decode-tokens 1 --warmup-runs 1 --measured-runs 3 --persistent-session --force-bulk-prefill --bulk-prefill-attention-mode bulk --use-wmma-prefill --use-gemv-decode --graph-replay-decode --compiler-version-file /tmp/hipengine-qwen36-27b-single-layout-hipcc-version.txt --require-cached-build --json <output>

rejected_subcandidate.change: Also size linear-attention route-exclusive scratch to 1024 rows and subchunk outer 4096-row linear layers.
rejected_subcandidate.first_failure: The initial 8K guard rejected a 4096-row linear launch against 1024-row scratch before launch.
rejected_subcandidate.decision: removed because the 2.94% 8K prefill regression violates the no-regression gate; existing outer-chunk scheduling and full-sized linear scratch remain unchanged

safeguards.dense_nextn_command: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 HIPENGINE_HIP_ARCH=gfx1100 HIPENGINE_COMPILER_VERSION_FILE=/tmp/hipengine-qwen36-27b-single-layout-hipcc-version.txt HIPENGINE_REQUIRE_CACHED_BUILD=1 uv run pytest -q tests/test_qwen35_gguf_mtp_e2e.py::test_dense_q4_k_m_nextn_transaction_and_provider_match_scalar_ar

cross_engine.llamacpp_hip_memory_status: hipEngine remains below llama.cpp HIP at 512 and 1K, but above HIP by 0.439 GiB at 4K and the standardized 8K diagnostic.
cross_engine.speed_status: All final prefill/decode changes versus the prior compact-QK matrix are within 0.171%; frozen 512/1K/4K gate status is unchanged.

decision: Retain the exact gate-plane alias. It removes 8.9375/18.75/20.625/20.625 MiB tracked and 11.160/17.965/21.750/21.547 MiB whole-device peak at 512/1K/4K/8K without a throughput, token, NextN transaction, lifecycle, or W7900 regression. Do not claim memory parity: Vulkan still leads by 0.394/0.587/1.089/1.090 GiB, so the objective remains open.
